We have the sense that our time in Missouri is coming to a close. One of my friends at work found out with less than 2 months left that he was going to be losing his job. and then we were told that our terms would not be extended past four years. I have just hit my third year, so I have one year to go. I have been applying for jobs and we are really wanting to move to Ohio to be closer to Lauren's family.

I have been applying to jobs in Missouri and Ohio because it's the two places we'd like to live. It seems like the perfect time to move because Winnie is a year old now and Lauren isn't pregnant, but we are waiting on the Lord. I asked him to put it on my heart to stop looking for jobs if we weren't supposed to go and for the last two months I've not gotten the sense that I'm supposed to stop.

We have been getting weary of waiting if I'm being honest. Morale is pretty low most days as we hope to hear back about a job. Time will tell. But we are ready to move out into our own place.

# June 12 2026

The Lord is so good. Recently, we received an \$1800 gift from a family member, allowing us to pay off our last credit card. Over the last year, God has enabled us to pay off \$30,000 of debt. This includes three credit cards and a car loan. Time and again, God has provided for us in ways that we never could have anticipated or bet on. In fact, I wrote down all the unforseen financial gifts since I graduated college and estimated the value to be over \$215,000 over 11 years.

My faith has been encouraged so much by this. Truly the Lord cares for his loved ones. He's teaching me the truth of Matthew 6, "Seek the kingdom of God above all else and he will give you everything you need." 

Many people would say to me, "It's not possible for your wife to quit her job when you have as much credit card debt as you have and you are on a biologist's salary. But I say, "Look at what my God can do." Our life this past year has been a testimony to the providence of God. We have had to make some hard decisions, like moving in with church family and selling a car, but way beyond these decisions, the Lord has provided unexpectedly and miraculously.

On another note, I was sad to find out recently that a paper I submitted to a journal from grad school was rejected by the journal editors. It was discouraging because I spent so much time after work hours trying to put it together. I believe the feedback and criticism of the paper had basis, though and I don't think God wants me to throw in the towel yet. We're going to have to revamp sections and find a different journal, but I am hoping the Lord provides the time and opportunity to work on this project and see it to completion. The news came at a good time as we have just arrived in Georgia for a wedding and travel to Tennessee next week for my sister's wedding. Some time in a cabin and with family should help with the discouragement and give me the motivation to keep going.

# March 07 2026

Back in the swing of things at work now. Because several people resigned last year, we have all been very busy with projects at work. As the weather warms, we ramp up field research and some days I almost forget to eat lunch.

Life at home has been good and hard. We are close to being able to move out on our own. Hopefully in the next two to five months we will be in a place financially to do so.

We thank God for his work in our lives. A verse that has been in my mind lately is Psalm 62:1, "I wait quietly for the Lord, for my victory comes from Him. He is my rock and my salvation, my fortress where I will not be shaken." This verse reminds me that no matter how busy life is, it is good to wait quietly for God and to spend time with him in busy seasons. Without him, all my efforts and progress will be for nothing.

# December 19 2025

I just got back from my first overnight field trip for work since Winnie was born. The trip, was a big test for my wife, especially considering she went to the ER over the weekend because of a supplement that didn't sit well with her stomach and caused a lot of pain.

We're getting ready to travel to Ohio for Christmas. For Thanksgiving we went to my parent's house in Knoxville, TN. This was a great time because so much of my family was there and they got to meet Winnie. We also sent off my younger brother to Argentina by laying hands on him and praying over him. It was an emotional moment and now he's officially moved to Argentina.

# November 15 2025

As of two days ago, I am now officially back at work. I originally went back to work September 29 after taking 8 weeks of paternity leave. But as soon as I got back to work, the government shut down because they failed to agree on a budget, so I was back home for another 6 weeks! This has been both very challenging and a great blessing. 

On the one hand, spending almost 15 weeks at home since Winifred was born has felt both boring and directionless. I've felt like a bum some days. I have to keep reminding myself that staying home with my family is a very good thing to be doing. That just because I'm not at work, doesn't mean I'm a bum. 

I intentionally chose not to pick up a second job during the shutdown. Last year, I picked up a second job to try to pay for wedding expenses--- that turned out to be something I regretted. I felt like I wasn't fully trusting God with my income. So this time around, even though I had free time at home, I chose to spend it with my wife and daughter instead of making some extra cash. I'm really glad I did because I know there may never be another time when I get to spend 15 uninterrupted weeks with my family.

We sold Lauren's car and my french horn, which were very hard decisions for both of us. She loved that car, it was her first car purchase. I played that horn from 5th/6th grade to senior in college. I loved it. But we have a shared vision of making the one income thing work and we felt like God was telling us to live simply to make that happen. And it's funny how God works sometimes. We didn't plan to get another car, but as soon as we sold our car, my sister asked us if we were in the market and said she'd sell us her 150k mile car for $1200! So Lauren is going to get a car after all. But it wasn't until she was willing to let go of it that God provided.


Overall, the shutdown was perfectly timed with our circumstance. Lauren was already feeling distant from the support of family since moving out to Missouri. Despite quitting her job and being a SAHM, she was worried how motherhood would go without any additional help. So to be able to support her extra in these early months has been an amazing blessing.

# September 17 2025

The last 5 weeks have been lots of time with my wife and daughter. It has been slow and good. We did travel 12 hours to Ohio when Winifred was just 3 weeks old because Lauren's brother was getting married. Maybe we're crazy, but I think it was worth it. Fortunately we were able to break up the trip so we weren't driving more than 4 hours each day. We stayed in Ohio for 2 weeks to recover then came back home. And yes, we're glad to be back!

![Having a picnic at a rest area on our way to Ohio.](/files/profiles/lauren.jpg){.lightbox fig-align="center" height=3in}\

Our daughter has been changing so much each week it seems. It's hard to believe, really.

We've started showing our faces a bit more, going to church and small group now. Though we don't last too long with the baby, we know it's good for us on a spiritual and relational level.

# August 10 2025

Our daughter has been born! She was born on August 3rd and she and my wife are doing really well a week later. We have had so many people show up in support of us including in-laws and the family we are living with right now in Missouri. From groceries, to meals, to gift cards for food --- my step-father-in-law even changed the oil in one of our cars to help out. 

We're trying to cherish this time right now just the three of us. I have some time off work over the next year (up to 12 weeks), so I'll be taking a large chunk of that time up front.

# July 29 2025

A lot has unfolded since I wrote an update. My wife is due any day now. She's been a trooper for her first time as a mother, having gone over her due date by 6 days now. Hang in there sweetie!

I still have my job, praise God. He has really taken care of our every need. A couple months ago we moved in with a family from our church and my wife resigned from her job because we both felt like that's what God was telling us in preparation for the baby coming.

It's been a summer of transition between the short distance move from Rocheport, MO to Harrisburg, MO (still in the Columbia, MO area). We are a little more cramped now, but God knew what we needed between saving money on rent and having closer connection with our community.


# March 8 2025

My wife is expecting in late July and we are very excited to be first-time parents!

Since moving to Missouri, our church family has been so generous to us, helping meet our every need---like helping us move from our apartment to new rental home and gifting us an AirBnB for no reason other than just needing a weekend escape.

With the recent federal [Reduction in Force (RIF) memorandum](https://www.chcoc.gov/content/guidance-agency-rif-and-reorganization-plans-requested-implementing-president%E2%80%99s-%E2%80%9Cdepartment) in effect, my wife and I are expecting that I will lose my job in the coming weeks/months.
